findings.title: update/destroy crash when record is not found
findings.body: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, `update` and `destroy` both look up the host with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without a nil check. When the id doesn't match an existing record, `host` is `nil`, and `save_host(nil)` raises `NoMethodError` on the next line (`host.host = …`) while `destroy` raises on `host.destroy`. A single bad PUT or DELETE (e.g., from a stale tab, bookmarked URL, or attacker probing the endpoint) takes down the request with a 500 instead of returning a clean 404/not-found response.

findings.title: No strong parameters and unfiltered raw mass assignment
findings.body: `save_host` reads `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` directly, with no strong-parameters whitelist and no presence check on the hash. An attacker submitting an empty body, a non-hash payload, or extra keys (e.g. `embeddable_host[created_at]=…`) triggers `NoMethodError` or, more importantly, can pass arbitrary `category_id` and overwrite the host attribute silently (the category_id validation is the only guard). Submitting a missing `:embeddable_host` key crashes the endpoint with a 500.

findings.title: SQL injection via string interpolation in migration
findings.body: The data migration inserts each embeddable host with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, …) VALUES ('#{h}', …)"`. The `h` value comes from the persisted `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` text column, which is admin-editable, so it can legitimately contain a single quote / semicolon / comment (e.g. `evil'); DROP TABLE users; --`). Interpolation, rather than `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`, executes that fragment verbatim during `db:migrate`. Anyone able to set the site setting before migration runs can break or alter the database.

findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category row is absent
findings.body: `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM … WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the subquery returns at least one row. On any install that never set the `embed_category` site setting (the common case after this PR removes the setting), `[0]` is `nil` and calling `['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration. The `if category_id == 0` fallback below only protects against a numeric zero, not against the `nil` array element.

findings.title: Server response never embeds the full EmbeddableHost objects, so client-side hydration produces undefined entries
findings.body: `EmbeddingSerializer` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, … embed: :ids`, so the JSON body only contains `embeddable_host_ids: [...]` – the host records themselves are NOT side-loaded in the response. On the client, `store.js` `_hydrateEmbedded` matches the new `(.+)_id(s?)$` regex and calls `_lookupSubType('embeddable_host', 'embedding', id, root)`. That helper looks up `root[this.pluralize('embeddable_host')]` (i.e. `root['embeddable_hosts']`), which does not exist, and (unlike `category`) there is no global cache for embeddable hosts, so the lookup returns `undefined` for every id. The result is that the rendered `embedding.embeddable_hosts` array is full of `undefined` – the admin Embedding page will appear empty (only the Add Host button shows), and any subsequent save/edit on those rows will throw when the component accesses `host.category` / `host.host`.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op that returns 200
findings.body: `EmbeddingController#update` just re-renders the current `@embedding` without ever reading the request body or persisting anything. The PUT route is wired up and the JSON adapter is configured to call it, so any client PUT (and the controller-level `saveChanges` action that calls `update({})`) will succeed silently. Worse, the misleading 200 response means a client bug can never be detected – nothing was saved but the caller is told everything was fine. This either should be removed or actually persist the requested changes.

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(/^https?:///, '')` directly on `self.host`. There is no `validates_presence_of :host` on the model and the database column is `null: false`, so a record constructed via `EmbeddableHost.new` (no attrs), `EmbeddableHost.new(host: nil)`, or one whose host gets blanked out in another callback will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` on save instead of producing a clean validation error. The controller happens to always assign a host, but the model itself isn't safe to use standalone.

findings.title: expandable_first_post? test no longer covers the embeddable_host condition
findings.body: After this PR removes `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` from `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, the test `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` and the surrounding `describe 'with an emeddable host'` block (which `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in its setup) only check `SiteSetting.embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?` – the embeddable_host presence is irrelevant. The 'no embeddable host' assertion now passes vacuously (it just checks the default SiteSetting + topic state) and would not catch a regression where someone re-introduces a host-presence requirement. The test setup and name should be updated to reflect the actual contract.

findings.title: category_id is silently dropped when no EmbeddableHost row matches the URL
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` now derives the category purely from `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`. If the host is not registered (typo in URL, race condition where an import races a host deletion, etc.), `eh.try(:category_id)` is `nil` and the post is created with no category, falling through to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` via Topic's callback. Previously the category came from `SiteSetting.embed_category` (always defined), so the new path silently funnels misclassified imports into uncategorized without any warning. The callers in `topic_retriever.rb` already short-circuit when the host is not allowed, so this is mostly correct, but a brief log/raise would catch data-pipeline bugs.
